description: Change of use of the C3 dwelling to a C4 HMO [retrospective]
decision_conditions: <p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed development results in the loss of a 2-bedroom family-sized dwellinghouse, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the development plan and supporting evidence base. While it would provide a dwelling in the form of an HMO, it fails to demonstrate that there is an identified need and would not be located in an area with a high level of access to public transport and is therefore not considered an appropriate location for an HMO.&nbsp; As such, the proposal is considered to have a detrimental impact on the borough's supply of family housing and is contrary to the following policies: - National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)- Policies D6, D14 and T4 of the London Plan (March 2021)- Policies SP3, SP8, DMD1, DMT1, DMH5 and DMSI3 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed development would fail to comply with the&nbsp; required minimum space standards for both the double bedrooms, built-in storage and the overall gross internal area required for 4 tenants and would therefore provide a substandard quality of accommodation detrimental to the standard of living of future residents. Therefore, the proposal fails to comply with:&nbsp; National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024); Policy D6 of the London Plan (March 2021); and&nbsp;&nbsp; Technical housing standards – nationally described space standard (March 2015)</span></p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed development fails to demonstrate that additional demand for parking from the development could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area.&nbsp; Especially as the application site has a low PTAL score of 2 indicating poor access to public transport. The proposal is therefore likely to exacerbate existing parking stress thus add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site. &nbsp;As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision:- National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)- Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)- Policy DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></p>
borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
